junction.description.junction.local.ai.c: Junction; local AI coding agent bridge for OpenClaw, Hermes, and Souveraine, goose, mimo-code and many more!
junction.contributes.configuration.title: Junction
junction.contributes.configuration.prope: Active local agent bridge.

Global follow-up mode. Per-bridge overrides: junction.openclaw.followUpMode, junction.hermes.followUpMode, junction.souveraine.followUpMode.
Compact chat stream with activity folded into summary accordions.
Timeline chat stream with chronological reasoning/activity flow. Also enables the orange theme.
Chat look and feel.
In timeline mode, collapse the timeline pill after thinking finishes. Users can reopen the pill manually.

Glyphs for the assistant-message feedback (up/down vote) buttons. Buttons appear only for bridges whose backend natively supports feedback.
Temporarily disabled. Future code rewind/checkpoint snapshots will live behind this setting.
Temporarily disabled. Fork stays available; Fork & rewind is hidden until code rewind is rebuilt.
Local UI preference for agent sandbox display. Applied only when the active bridge supports a matching control surface.
Local UI preference for approval display. Applied only when the active bridge supports a matching control surface.
Enable Pretext-powered extra-rich text rendering with animated text effects (matrix scroll, typewriter, etc.). Uses canvas-based text layout for smoother animations.
Use the bundled "Good Fonts" pack — Comic Neue for regular text and Liga Comic Mono for monospace/code.
Follow the VS Code editor.wordWrap setting.
Never wrap tool output lines.
Always wrap tool output lines.
Word wrapping for tool pill output.
Show CodeLens actions above TODO/FIXME/HACK comments to send them to Junction.
Always show the context-usage chip/gauge, even at low usage. When off, it appears only once the context window is meaningfully full (~50%).
Show the vertical guide line beside activity rows in timeline mode.
Group consecutive file edits into compact sections (one per file) instead of showing each edit as a separate row.
Colored status dots (green success, red error, blinking while running)
Neutral dots with a spinner while running
Status indicator style on activity rows.
User message bubble corner radius. 0 = hard edges, 16 = default round, 999 = fully circular.
No pointed tip — full round corners
Pointed tip at top-right corner
Pointed tip at bottom-right corner
Position of the pointed tail on user message bubbles.
Custom keybinding to steer in-flight runs (e.g., 'Ctrl+Shift+Enter'). Left empty by default (unbound).
Show full chat history on load (locally installed OpenClaw instances only). When enabled, loads up to 1000 messages instead of the default 200. May be slower on large sessions.
Automatically stage active editor context when switching files. Explicit file pills are still sent normally.
Interval (in ms) for automatically staging editor context.
WebSocket URL of the OpenClaw runtime.
Path to the openclaw.json config file for the selected OpenClaw runtime.
Show every configured agent in the environment picker. When off (default), only each gateway's primary agent (the first entry in its config agents.list) is shown; child/extra agents are hidden.
Follow-up mode for OpenClaw. 'default' uses the global junction.followUpMode.
Local Hermes dashboard URL used for native WebSocket integration.
Local Hermes dashboard JSON-RPC WebSocket URL.
Local Hermes API server URL for explicit apiserver mode/status.
Hermes home used for the managed hermling test runtime.
Path to the hermes-agent repo for managed spawn (leave empty to disable managed spawn).
Path to a built `hermes` CLI to spawn the dashboard with (e.g. ~/bin/hermes). Empty = auto-detect: repoPath/venv/bin/hermes, else `hermes` on PATH.
Which Hermes surface to use. 'auto' uses the dashboard (full native features); 'dashboard' forces the WebSocket dashboard; 'apiserver' forces the API server (chat/models only).
API-server key override. Empty = read from the Hermes config.yaml (platforms.api_server.extra.key) or .env (API_SERVER_KEY).
Follow-up mode for Hermes. 'default' uses the global junction.followUpMode.
Local Souveraine HTTP server URL.
HOME directory used for the managed souvieling test runtime.
Path to the Souveraine repo for managed spawn (leave empty to disable managed spawn).
Follow-up mode for Souveraine. 'default' uses the global junction.followUpMode.
Connect to an already-running MiMoCode server (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8080). Leave empty to let Junction spawn and manage its own instance.
Path to the mimo binary. Use "mimo" if it is on PATH, or set the full path (e.g. /home/user/bin/mimo).
Port for the managed MiMoCode server (0 = auto-assign random port). Ignored when junction.mimocode.serverUrl is set.
MiMoCode data directory. Empty auto-discovers the installed MiMoCode profile.
MiMoCode follow-up mode preference (overrides junction.followUpMode when active bridge is MiMoCode)
Legacy goosed server URL. Native goose support uses the CLI transport.
Goose data directory. Leave empty for auto-detection (~/.goose).
Path to goose binary. Leave empty to auto-detect from PATH.
Optional dotenv file loaded into managed goose CLI runs. Leave empty to auto-detect a local hermLing env file when present.
Legacy goosed secret key. Native goose support uses the CLI transport.
Connect to an already-running `opencode serve` (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:4096). Leave empty to let Junction spawn and manage its own opencode server.
Path to the opencode binary. Leave empty to auto-detect (~/bin/opencode, then PATH).
Port for the managed opencode server (0 = auto-assign). Ignored when junction.opencode.serverUrl is set.
opencode config home (sets OPENCODE_CONFIG). Leave empty for the opencode default (~/.config/opencode).
Follow-up mode for opencode. 'default' uses the global junction.followUpMode.
Path to the built Pi coding-agent CLI entrypoint (dist/cli.js). Empty auto-detects a local source checkout when present.
HOME directory for managed Pi RPC runs. Empty uses the current process HOME.
Follow-up mode for Pi. 'default' uses the global junction.followUpMode.
OpenHands app server URL. Junction will spawn the managed server (junction.openhands.binaryPath) if this URL is unreachable.
Path to the openhands server launcher. Leave empty to auto-detect (~/bin/openhands).
OpenHands data/home directory (sets OPENHANDS_HOME). Leave empty for the OpenHands default (~/.openhands).
Path to the openhands repo for managed spawn (cwd for the launcher).
Follow-up mode for OpenHands. 'default' uses the global junction.followUpMode.
